highlights.title: Show HN: OzBrain, a shared brain for knowledge between agents and your team
highlights.summary: OzBrain is a shared knowledge hub for AI agents and teams, offering a central, app‑agnostic store that tracks, audits, resolves conflicts, and token‑optimizes agent‑generated content.
highlights.detail: It replaces human‑centric note tools by capturing all agent reasoning, allowing multiple collaborators to share and audit brains, and breaking knowledge into token‑friendly chunks for efficient indexing.

highlights.title: aaif-goose/goose
highlights.summary: goose is an open‑source Rust AI agent that can install, execute, edit, and test code using any LLM.
highlights.detail: The extensible framework lets developers plug in different language models and define custom toolchains, turning the agent into a versatile code‑assistant beyond simple suggestions.

highlights.title: abseil/abseil-cpp
highlights.summary: Abseil‑cpp provides a collection of common C++ libraries maintained by Google.
highlights.detail: The repository includes utilities for strings, time, synchronization, and more, offering production‑ready components that complement the C++ standard library.

highlights.title: affaan-m/ECC
highlights.summary: ECC is an agent harness performance‑optimization system that adds skills, instincts, memory, security, and research‑first development support for Claude Code, Codex, Opencode, Cursor, and other tools.
highlights.detail: The harness aims to improve LLM agent efficiency by integrating modular capabilities. It is positioned as a research‑first framework for developers building AI‑augmented applications. No licensing or release version is specified in the announcement.

items.title: Model: huihui-ai/Huihui-Qwen3.8-27B-abliterated-GGUF
items.summary: The Huihui‑Qwen3.8‑27B‑abliterated GGUF model supports image‑to‑text tasks and has been downloaded 635,416 times on Hugging Face.
items.detail: Designed for multimodal workloads, the model combines a 27‑billion‑parameter backbone with a quantized GGUF format, making it suitable for edge deployment while attracting substantial community interest.

items.title: Model: ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-GGUF
items.summary: Ornith‑1.5‑35B‑A3B GGUF is a text‑generation model with 173,935 downloads on Hugging Face.
items.detail: The model targets large‑scale language generation, offering an A3B architecture variant that balances quality and inference speed, and has gathered notable community engagement.

items.title: 555 Makes a Useful Beat Frequency Oscillator
items.summary: A 555 timer circuit is repurposed as a beat‑frequency oscillator for ham‑radio applications.
items.detail: The oscillator provides a low‑cost method to generate the audio‑frequency beat needed for certain digital modes, extending the utility of inexpensive hobbyist rigs.

items.title: An Atari Desktop On A Sega
items.summary: A Sega console has been modified to run an Atari‑style desktop environment using a -nommu Linux port.
items.detail: The project demonstrates that 16‑bit hardware can host familiar operating systems, leveraging the console’s existing video and input peripherals for a retro computing experience.

items.title: Open-Source ExpressLRS Receiver Reaches for Range
items.summary: An open‑source ExpressLRS receiver design improves range while operating with ≤1 W transmitter power.
items.detail: By optimizing antenna layout and firmware parameters, the receiver extends link distances for drones, showcasing the efficiency of the ExpressLRS protocol under strict power limits.

items.title: Sleeper E-bike has Solenoid Display
items.summary: A retro‑styled e‑bike conversion adds a solenoid‑actuated display to a classic road bike.
items.detail: The solenoid display provides a minimalist readout for speed and battery status, blending vintage aesthetics with modern electric‑assist technology.

items.title: The Shutter Makes This 3D Printed Camera Special
items.summary: A 3D‑printed camera uses a custom shutter mechanism to enable film exposure.
items.detail: The printable shutter allows precise timing for each frame, making analog photography accessible to makers without requiring machined metal parts.

items.title: You Gotta Want It
items.summary: A Hackaday feature revisits a classic educational toy that inspired many engineers.
items.detail: The article highlights the toy’s design principles and its role in fostering early interest in electronics and programming among a generation of hobbyists.

items.title: anthropics/claude-plugins-community
items.summary: Claude‑plugins‑community is a community‑maintained marketplace hosting plugins for Claude Cowork and Claude Code, with a read‑only mirror and submission portal at clau.de/plugin-directory-submission.
items.detail: The repository aggregates community contributions, simplifying discovery of extensions that enhance Claude's capabilities. It mirrors metadata only and encourages developers to submit via the provided form. No licensing details are listed.

items.title: block/buzz
items.summary: Buzz is a Rust‑based hive‑mind communication platform enabling distributed agents to exchange messages.
items.detail: The project targets collaborative AI workflows where multiple instances share context, focusing on low‑latency messaging and scalability across nodes. Documentation is minimal, and the repository does not specify a license or version.

items.title: browser-use/browser-harness
items.summary: Browser‑Harness is a Python self‑healing harness that lets large language models control a browser to perform arbitrary tasks.
items.detail: The harness monitors page state and can automatically recover from errors, allowing LLMs to continue execution without external intervention. It aims to generalize web automation for AI agents. No release version or licensing information is provided.
